courts.name: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
courts.note: Established by the Protocol (art. 1), in force 25 January 2004 (au.int). It complements the Commission's protective mandate (art. 2). Jurisdiction: cases on the interpretation and application of the Charter, the Protocol and other human rights instruments ratified by the States concerned; it decides disputes over its own jurisdiction (art. 3). Cases may be brought by the Commission, States parties in the roles listed and African intergovernmental organisations (art. 5(1)); individuals and NGOs with observer status before the Commission only against a State that has made an art. 34(6) declaration (arts. 5(3), 34(6)). On admissibility it applies Charter art. 56, may ask the Commission's opinion, and may consider cases or transfer them to the Commission (art. 6). Its judgment is final and not subject to appeal (art. 28(2)). Art. 30: States parties undertake to comply with judgments in cases to which they are parties and to guarantee execution. That is a duty of the parties to a case, not a rule that decisions bind national courts or later cases; the Protocol states no such rule, so no relation or precedent entry is recorded. valid_from is the Protocol's entry into force.

courts.name: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
courts.note: Established within the OAU by Charter art. 30 to promote and protect human and peoples' rights in Africa; art. 45 sets its functions (promotion, protection, interpreting the Charter on request, tasks from the Assembly). It hears communications from States (arts. 47-49) and other communications (arts. 55-56). Its findings are made as recommendations: it reports the facts and its findings to the States concerned and the Assembly (art. 52) and may make to the Assembly 'such recommendations as it deems useful' (art. 53); where communications reveal serious or massive violations, the Assembly may request a factual report with findings and recommendations (art. 58); measures stay confidential, and reports are published, only as the Assembly decides (art. 59). It may submit cases to the Court (Protocol art. 5(1)(a)) and the Court may transfer cases to it (Protocol art. 6(3)). valid_from is the Charter's entry into force (au.int); members are elected after that date (art. 64(1)).
